Dressed state

Words: 191 Articles: 2
Quantum system OurBigBook.com
An eigenstate of an interacting system that combines degrees of freedom which would be separate in the uncoupled model.

Atom-field dressed state

Words: 173 Articles: 1
Dressed state OurBigBook.com
A dressed state of an atom and its driving field. Within the rotating-wave approximation, the paired configurations ∣e,n⟩ and ∣g,n+1⟩ mix. A classical-drive rotating-frame Hamiltonian H=ℏ(−Δσz​+Ωσx​)/2 has eigenvalues ±ℏΔ2+Ω2​/2. At resonance its eigenvectors are equal-weight combinations of the two bare configurations. Radiative transitions between neighboring manifolds explain the Mollow triplet.

Mollow triplet

Words: 129
Atom-field dressed state OurBigBook.com
A central peak and two sidebands in the resonance fluorescence spectrum of a sufficiently strongly driven two-level system. The atom-field dressed state splitting produces sidebands near ωL​±Ω2+Δ2​, where Ω is the resonant Rabi frequency. On resonance, changing the drive intensity changes the sideband spacing. Damping and detection conditions determine the resolved line shapes; the elastic coherent contribution must be distinguished from inelastic fluorescence.[ref]
An experimental test drives an isolated transition with a narrow-band laser, collects fluorescence away from the intense drive beam, and scans a spectral analyzer while varying drive power. Resolving the sidebands requires spectral resolution and coupling frequency sufficient relative to the radiative linewidth. The predicted spectrum concerns transitions of the coupled system rather than simply the time dependence of its population.

Quantum state (ρ)

Words: 12k Articles: 111
Quantum system OurBigBook.com
A quantum state describes a preparation through its predicted measurement in quantum mechanics probabilities. In the Hilbert space formulation, a pure state is a quantum state ray: a normalized vector representative ∣ψ⟩ satisfies ⟨ψ∣ψ⟩=1, and representatives differing by a global phase describe the same quantum state. [ref]
Both pure states and mixed states are represented by a density operator on the chosen complex Hilbert space:
ρ=ρ†,⟨v∣ρ∣v⟩≥0 for every ∣v⟩,Trρ=1.
(1)
Thus ρ is Hermitian, positive semidefinite and of unit trace; in infinite dimension it must also be a trace-class operator. For a normalized pure state, ρ=∣ψ⟩⟨ψ∣ is a rank-one orthogonal projection. A mixed state has no single such vector representative. Its density matrix is the matrix of ρ in a chosen orthonormal basis. [ref] For a discrete POVM with effects Ea​≥0 and ∑a​Ea​=I, the Born rule reads
P(a)=Tr(ρEa​),P(a)=⟨ψ∣Ea​∣ψ⟩ for a pure state.
(2)
These constraints and Born rule probabilities describe arbitrary finite-dimensional preparations. [ref]
Randomly choosing normalized pure states with probabilities wj​ and forgetting the label gives
ρ=∑j​wj​∣ψj​⟩⟨ψj​∣,wj​≥0,∑j​wj​=1.
(3)
This quantum state ensemble averages probabilities; a quantum superposition adds probability amplitudes. Several ensembles can give the same density operator. Quantum entanglement can make a reduced density matrix mixed while the joint quantum state is pure. [ref]
The preparation, the choice of basis, and the measurement are separate ingredients. A wavefunction ψ(x)=⟨x∣ψ⟩ is the position representation of a pure state; a general mixed state requires a density operator. For a closed quantum system, a unitary operator evolves it as ρ↦UρU†, preserving its eigenvalues and purity of a density operator. [ref] The Bloch sphere and Bloch ball give the qubit geometry; quantum state tomography connects repeated preparations to an estimated density matrix; projective measurement treats the conditional state after an outcome.

Gaussian quantum state

Words: 122 Articles: 2
Quantum state OurBigBook.com
A bosonic state with Gaussian phase-space characteristic function, specified by its first and second optical quadrature moments. Vacuum, coherent states, optical squeezed vacuum and thermal states are examples. Gaussian here describes phase-space statistics, not a Gaussian optical pulse envelope.

Number-conserving Gaussian quantum state

Words: 56
Gaussian quantum state OurBigBook.com
Here number-conserving means invariant under a global particle-number quantum phase rotation: the field mean and anomalous averages ⟨ψψ⟩ vanish. It does not mean a sharp total particle number. All normal correlations are obtained by Wick pairings of the one-body density matrix. Independent thermal bosonic modes satisfy this rule; generic nonvacuum bosonic number states do not. A Slater determinant is the analogous fermionic pairing state.

Squeezed thermal state (V1,2​=(2nth​+1)e∓2r/4)

Words: 35
Gaussian quantum state OurBigBook.com
Applying a single-mode squeeze operator to a thermal state gives the displayed principal optical-quadrature variances. Their uncertainty product exceeds the pure-state minimum when nth​>0. Sufficient squeezing is needed to put the quiet optical quadrature below the vacuum reference.

Quantum state ray ([ψ]={λ∣ψ⟩:λ∈C∖{0}})

Words: 114
Quantum state OurBigBook.com
A quantum state ray is the equivalence class of nonzero vectors in a complex Hilbert space under multiplication by a nonzero complex number. Its span is a one-dimensional linear subspace, but the zero vector is not a state representative. A unit vector fixes the norm and leaves a global phase free. [ref]
For a nonzero representative ∣v⟩, the associated pure state density operator is
ρ[v]​=⟨v∣v⟩∣v⟩⟨v∣​.
(4)
Replacing ∣v⟩ by λ∣v⟩ multiplies both numerator and denominator by ∣λ∣2, so the quotient is unchanged. In particular, for every POVM effect E,
⟨eiγψ∣E∣eiγψ⟩=e−iγeiγ⟨ψ∣E∣ψ⟩=⟨ψ∣E∣ψ⟩.
(5)
This proves that a global phase changes no measurement probability. Changing the relative quantum phase of two nonzero components can change the density operator, as the following comparison shows.

Coherent preparation and incoherent mixing

Words: 373
Quantum state OurBigBook.com
Choose the qubit computational basis ∣0⟩,∣1⟩, also called the Z basis, and the Hadamard basis ∣±⟩=(∣0⟩±∣1⟩)/2​, also called the X basis. Compare a coherent preparation of ∣+⟩ with choosing ∣0⟩ or ∣1⟩ at random with equal probabilities and discarding that label:
ρ+​=21​(11​11​),ρmix​=21​∣0⟩⟨0∣+21​∣1⟩⟨1∣=21​(10​01​).
(6)
These are original ideal preparation models. Their Z-basis probabilities are both (1/2,1/2), because their quantum state populations agree. Their X-basis probabilities are respectively (1,0) and (1/2,1/2). Indeed ⟨+∣ρ+​∣+⟩=1, whereas ⟨+∣I/2∣+⟩=1/2. The missing off-diagonal quantum coherence therefore changes a prediction that the common populations cannot determine.
For a relative quantum phase ϕ, the coherent family instead has
∣ψϕ​⟩=2​∣0⟩+eiϕ∣1⟩​,ρϕ​=21​(1eiϕ​e−iϕ1​),PX​(±)=21±cosϕ​.
(7)
The last formula follows by adding or subtracting the two probability amplitudes before taking the squared modulus. At ϕ=π, the state is ∣−⟩ and the X outcomes switch to (0,1), while the Z outcomes remain (1/2,1/2). In contrast, −∣+⟩ changes both components by the same global phase and retains the X outcomes (1,0). In photon polarization, the identification ∣0⟩=∣H⟩, ∣1⟩=∣V⟩ makes ∣+⟩ and ∣−⟩ the two orthogonal diagonal linear polarizations; these labels describe measurement bases, not spatial axes for photon spin.
Even perfect statistics in one basis cannot certify a preparation. The above Z data fit both density matrices. Conversely, distinct preparation histories can yield the same quantum state:
21​∣0⟩⟨0∣+21​∣1⟩⟨1∣=21​∣+⟩⟨+∣+21​∣−⟩⟨−∣=2I​.
(8)
The off-diagonal terms cancel in the right-hand ensemble. Every measurement on the qubit alone then has identical probabilities for those two histories. A retained classical label would allow conditioning on different members of the quantum state ensemble; it is extra information beyond the unlabelled density operator.

Polarization preparation and dephasing experiment

Words: 169
Quantum state OurBigBook.com
A 2018 photonic experiment makes the distinction between populations and quantum coherence controllable. A 400-nm laser pumped a crystal to generate paired photons, filtered near 800 nm. One photon triggered collection; the other entered the apparatus. A half-wave plate and polarizing beam splitter selected horizontal photon polarization; another half-wave plate prepared balanced H,V quantum superpositions. Separated polarization paths and diffraction gratings let a spatial light modulator control their frequency-dependent quantum phases and spectral weights. Recombined paths passed through quartz plates whose adjustable thickness controlled polarization–frequency coupling. Quarter- and half-wave plates plus a polarizing beam splitter selected tomography bases; jointly registered photodetector events supplied the readout. Quantum state tomography inferred polarization density matrices at each thickness. The dephasing model preserves diagonal populations while changing off-diagonal quantum coherence. Here the unobserved photon frequency acts as the environment for the polarization qubit. Finite modulator resolution and imperfect spectral shaping limited agreement with the intended dynamics; this experiment does not establish exact I/2 preparation or the ideal probabilities above. [ref]

Dicke state (∣Dmn​⟩)

Words: 217 Articles: 2
Quantum state OurBigBook.com
The n-qubit Dicke state with m excitations is the normalized equal superposition
∣Dmn​⟩=(mn​)−1/2∑∣x∣=m​∣x⟩,0≤m≤n,
(9)
where ∣x∣ is the Hamming weight in the computational basis. The binomial coefficient counts the mutually orthogonal summands, proving normalization. Every permutation of the qubits leaves the vector unchanged. Splitting the sum according to the first bit and using (mn−1​)/(mn​)=(n−m)/n gives
∣Dmn​⟩=nn−m​​∣0⟩∣Dmn−1​⟩+nm​​∣1⟩∣Dm−1n−1​⟩.
(10)
Terms with zero coefficient are omitted at the endpoints. This recursion is useful for partial traces and for distributing a logical qubit among many symmetric physical qubits.

W state (∣Wn​⟩=∣D1n​⟩)

Words: 56
Dicke state OurBigBook.com
The n-qubit W state is the Dicke state with one excitation:
∣Wn​⟩=n​1​∑j=1n​∣0⋯010⋯0⟩=∣D1n​⟩.
(11)
For three qubits it is (∣001⟩+∣010⟩+∣100⟩)/3​. Its reduced density matrix on any one qubit is diag((n−1)/n,1/n), from the Dicke state recursion. For n>1 both diagonal entries are nonzero, so that qubit is entangled with the rest: a pure product state would have a pure marginal. A symmetric-arm reduction of an exchange Hamiltonian supplies a dynamical preparation from one initial excitation.

One-qubit reduction of Dicke-state superpositions (ρ01​=αβ∗(n−m)(m+1)​/n)

Words: 80
Dicke state OurBigBook.com
For ∣Ω⟩=α∣Dmn​⟩+β∣Dm+1n​⟩, ∣α∣2+∣β∣2=1 and 0≤m<n, the reduced density matrix of any one qubit is
ρ=n1​((n−m)∣α∣2+(n−m−1)∣β∣2(n−m)(m+1)​α∗β​(n−m)(m+1)​αβ∗m∣α∣2+(m+1)∣β∣2​).
(12)
Use the Dicke state recursion. The rest-of-system vectors of different Hamming weights are orthogonal. For the diagonal terms this leaves the probabilities of the distinguished bit being zero and one. In the cross term, only the rest vector ∣Dmn−1​⟩ occurs in both states, with coefficients (n−m)/n​ multiplying ∣0⟩ and (m+1)/n​ multiplying ∣1⟩. Thus Trrest​(∣Dmn​⟩⟨Dm+1n​∣)=(n−m)(m+1)​∣0⟩⟨1∣/n, proving the matrix. A single Dicke state alone gives the diagonal matrix diag((n−m)/n,m/n).

Flavor eigenstate

Words: 49
Quantum state OurBigBook.com
A flavor eigenstate is a state with a definite flavor label in the specified interaction or flavor-charge basis. For neutral kaons, K0=dsˉ and Kˉ0=sdˉ have definite opposite strangeness. Weak interactions mix them, so these flavor states are not the mass eigenstates. The precise flavor basis must be specified when discussing mixing.

Quantum superposition (∣ψ⟩=∑j​aj​∣j⟩,∑j​∣aj​∣2=1)

Words: 390 Articles: 3
Quantum state OurBigBook.com
A quantum superposition is a linear combination of quantum state vectors in a complex Hilbert space. In a specified orthonormal basis, a normalized pure state has the displayed expansion, where aj​ are probability amplitudes. A nonzero linear combination can always be normalized; an arbitrary sum of normalized vectors need not already have norm one. Having more than one nonzero component depends on the chosen basis: the Hadamard basis vector ∣+⟩ is a quantum superposition of the two computational-basis states, but is a single vector of the Hadamard basis. [ref].
The distinction from classical ignorance is quantitative. Consider the normalized qubit quantum state
∣ψϕ​⟩=23​​∣0⟩+2eiϕ​∣1⟩.
(13)
Its density operator, written in the computational basis, is
ρϕ​=∣ψϕ​⟩⟨ψϕ​∣=(3/4(3​/4)eiϕ​(3​/4)e−iϕ1/4​).
(14)
Preparing ∣0⟩ with probability 3/4 and ∣1⟩ with probability 1/4, while discarding the preparation label, instead gives the mixed state
ρmix​=43​∣0⟩⟨0∣+41​∣1⟩⟨1∣=(3/40​01/4​).
(15)
The diagonal entries agree, so both preparations give the same computational-basis measurement probabilities. The off-diagonal entries of ρϕ​ retain quantum coherence and the relative quantum phase. In the Hadamard basis, the Born rule gives
⟨±∣ρmix​∣±⟩=21​,⟨±∣ρϕ​∣±⟩=21​±43​​cosϕ.
(16)
The density matrix representation retains this distinction between a pure state and a mixed state. [ref].
For example, at ϕ=0, the quantum superposition yields the plus outcome with probability about 0.9330, whereas the mixed state yields it with probability 0.5. At ϕ=π/2 these particular probabilities agree, although the density matrices still differ: equality for one measurement does not establish equality of quantum states. The probability amplitude figure shows the comparison throughout a full cycle of relative quantum phase.
This is why a quantum superposition is useful: quantum gates act linearly on its probability amplitudes, and unitary operators preserve the full pure state information, including relative quantum phases. A Hadamard gate can turn otherwise hidden quantum coherence into different outcome probabilities. The beautiful feature is that the same basis weights can support different predictions when amplitudes recombine. The expansion specifies a preparation and its measurement predictions; it does not assign every unmeasured outcome a simultaneous classical value. See projective measurement for the separate question of the conditional state after a measurement.

Quantum interference

Words: 86 Articles: 2
Quantum superposition OurBigBook.com
Quantum interference occurs when probability amplitudes for indistinguishable alternatives combine before the Born rule assigns probabilities.
Period of two-state quantum interference (T=2πℏ/∣E2​−E1​∣)
Words: 42
Quantum interference OurBigBook.com
A superposition of two distinct energy eigenstates gives the expectation value of a time-independent observable an interference term proportional to e−i(E2​−E1​)t/ℏ. The displayed beat period applies when that term has nonzero amplitude. A vanishing off-diagonal matrix element, zero state coefficient or equal energies instead gives a constant expectation value.
Hong-Ou-Mandel effect
Words: 34
Quantum interference OurBigBook.com
Two indistinguishable bosons entering separate inputs of an ideal balanced beam splitter have zero probability of leaving one per output. The two alternatives for that occupancy interfere destructively. Distinguishability in temporal, spatial or internal modes weakens the cancellation.

Qudit (Cd)

Words: 65 Articles: 1
Quantum state OurBigBook.com
A qudit is a quantum subsystem with d distinguishable basis states and Hilbert space Cd. A qubit is the special case d=2. Tensor products of qudits give a natural setting for local Hamiltonians and finite-dimensional quantum circuits.

Qudit shift and phase operators (X∣j⟩=∣j+1⟩,Z∣j⟩=ωj∣j⟩)

Words: 33
Qudit OurBigBook.com
For an n-level qudit and primitive root of unity ω, these unitary operators obey Xn=Zn=I and ZX=ωXZ. The inverse of XsZ−r is ZrX−s, with the order reversed. These operators implement the receiver corrections in qudit teleportation.

Qubit (H≅C2)

Words: 1k Articles: 1
Quantum state OurBigBook.com
A qubit, or quantum bit, is a quantum system whose state space is a two-dimensional complex Hilbert space. Choose an orthonormal basis ∣0⟩,∣1⟩, called the computational basis. A pure state has a normalized representative ∣ψ⟩=α∣0⟩+β∣1⟩, where α,β are complex probability amplitudes and ∣α∣2+∣β∣2=1. General qubit states, including mixed states, require a density matrix. [ref].
The abstract qubit describes the chosen degree of freedom: for spin one-half, ∣0⟩,∣1⟩ can label spin up and down along a specified axis; for photon polarization in a fixed propagation mode, they can label horizontal and vertical polarization, ∣H⟩,∣V⟩. These implementations share the same two-dimensional linear algebra, but their preparation and measurement in quantum mechanics use different apparatus. A qubit therefore need not be an entire two-level particle. [ref].
The usefulness of a qubit lies in controlling quantum superpositions and their relative quantum phases, then converting them into outcome probabilities with quantum gates and an appropriate measurement. One ideal computational-basis measurement returns one label, zero or one. It does not reveal both probability amplitudes, their relative quantum phase, or all the bits of a larger register's expansion. Quantum state tomography instead estimates a qubit state using many repetitions of the preparation and suitable measurement settings. [ref].
An actual preparation and measurement example is Dederick and Beck's 2014 teaching-laboratory experiment. A 405-nm laser pumped two nonlinear crystals, producing signal and idler photons near 810 nm. In their non-entangled run the source produced ∣H⟩s​∣H⟩i​; a quarter-wave plate in the signal arm changed its photon polarization to ∣L⟩=(∣H⟩+i∣V⟩)/2​ in their convention. The plate supplies a relative quantum phase between polarization components. An idler detection selected the signal trials; signal detectors measured horizontal/vertical, diagonal, and circular polarization bases on separate runs. Before the polarization analyzer, a half-wave plate at 22.5 degrees selected the diagonal basis, and a quarter-wave plate at 45 degrees selected the circular basis. Coincidence counts NAB​,NAB′​ gave the conditional positive-outcome frequency NAB​/(NAB​+NAB′​). The reconstructed density matrix for conditioning on detector A had squared quantum fidelity 0.96 with ∣L⟩ and purity of a density operator 0.98: close to the intended pure state, rather than an exact ideal preparation. [ref].
The model diagram explains why those settings matter. With ∣0⟩=∣H⟩ and ∣1⟩=∣V⟩, the intended ∣L⟩ gives equal probabilities in both the horizontal/vertical computational basis and diagonal Hadamard basis, just as the mixed state I/2 does. In the circular basis ∣±i⟩=(∣0⟩±i∣1⟩)/2​, however, the ideal ∣L⟩=∣+i⟩ always gives the plus outcome, whereas I/2 still gives equal probabilities. These are deductions from the Born rule, not the paper's measured counts. Unequal detector efficiencies and finite samples must be accounted for when interpreting experimental frequencies; the ideal comparison assumes equally efficient detection.

Qubit state (ρ=21​(I+r⋅σ))

Words: 647
Qubit OurBigBook.com
A qubit state specifies measurement probabilities, rather than a pre-existing answer to every possible measurement. For a pure state, normalized vectors differing by a global phase represent the same physical state:
∣ψ⟩∼eiγ∣ψ⟩,γ∈R.
(17)
Equivalently, the pure state is a ray: the one-dimensional complex linear subspace spanned by any nonzero representative. Dividing a nonzero vector by its norm fixes its length, but leaves the global phase free. The density operator is unchanged because (eiγ∣ψ⟩)(eiγ∣ψ⟩)†=∣ψ⟩⟨ψ∣. In contrast, multiplying only one nonzero component by eiϕ changes a relative quantum phase and can change measurement probabilities. [ref].
After choosing a global phase, every pure state of a qubit can be written
∣ψ(θ,ϕ)⟩=cos(θ/2)∣0⟩+eiϕsin(θ/2)∣1⟩,0≤θ≤π,0≤ϕ<2π.
(18)
At θ=0 or π, the parameter ϕ does not distinguish physical states: only one component survives. Elsewhere it is the relative quantum phase. The corresponding unit Bloch vector is r=(sinθcosϕ,sinθsinϕ,cosθ) on the existing Bloch sphere. Its angles describe a space of states; for a photon polarization qubit they are not the photon's position or direction of travel. [ref].
The Born rule in the computational basis gives P(0)=cos2(θ/2) and P(1)=sin2(θ/2). These probabilities discard ϕ. In the Hadamard basis ∣±⟩=(∣0⟩±∣1⟩)/2​, adding or subtracting the probability amplitudes instead gives
PX​(±)=21​∣α±β∣2=21​±Re(α∗β)=21​(1±sinθcosϕ).
(19)
This last equality follows by substituting the angular representative. In the basis ∣±i⟩=(∣0⟩±i∣1⟩)/2​, the same calculation gives
PY​(±)=21​∣α∓iβ∣2=21​±Im(α∗β)=21​(1±sinθsinϕ).
(20)
Thus both the real and imaginary parts of quantum coherence can be observed, using different measurement settings. For example, (∣0⟩+∣1⟩)/2​ and (∣0⟩−∣1⟩)/2​ both give P(0)=P(1)=1/2, but the first gives PX​(+)=1 and the second PX​(+)=0. A global phase could never cause this difference.
For a general qubit state, write its density matrix in the computational basis as
ρ=(pc∗​c1−p​),p∈R,c∈C,0≤p≤1,∣c∣2≤p(1−p).
(21)
These are exactly the Hermitian, unit-trace, positive semidefinite constraints. Positivity means every eigenvalue is nonnegative, not that every matrix entry is nonnegative. The general definition is given in density matrix. [ref].
For this two-by-two matrix, the explicit constraint follows from its determinant, detρ=p(1−p)−∣c∣2: with trace one, a nonnegative determinant and real eigenvalues rule out a negative eigenvalue. Its eigenvalues are
λ±​=21​(1±(2p−1)2+4∣c∣2​).
(22)
The pure states have ∣c∣2=p(1−p) and eigenvalues 1,0; the mixed states have strict inequality and two positive eigenvalues. For a normalized representative, p=∣α∣2 and c=αβ∗. A complete set of commuting observables consists of mutually commuting quantum observables whose joint eigenvalues distinguish all vectors of a simultaneous eigenbasis, up to phase. An additional quantum observable that is already a function of the others supplies no independent quantum number.
For the addition of angular momentum, the uncoupled labels (j1​,j2​,m1​,m2​) correspond to {J12​,J22​,J1z​,J2z​}, whereas the coupled labels (j1​,j2​,j,m) correspond to {J12​,J22​,J2,Jz​}. The expectation value of a quantum observable is the expected value of its measurement outcome random variable in a specified quantum state. It predicts the mean of outcomes from many identical quantum state preparations. It need not equal any one possible outcome: for a spin one-half particle, equal probabilities of +ℏ/2 and −ℏ/2 give mean zero even though zero is never an outcome of that spin component. Here ℏ is the reduced Planck constant.
Let A=A† be a Hermitian operator on a finite-dimensional Hilbert space, and let ∣ψ⟩ be a normalized pure state, ⟨ψ∣ψ⟩=1. The spectral theorem writes
A=∑r​ar​Pr​,Pr​Ps​=δrs​Pr​,∑r​Pr​=I.
(27)
The ar​ are distinct real eigenvalues, Pr​ are orthogonal projections onto their eigenspaces, and I is the identity operator. For an ideal projective measurement of A, the Born rule and the expectation value give
pr​=⟨ψ∣Pr​∣ψ⟩=∥Pr​∣ψ⟩∥2,∑r​pr​=1,⟨A⟩ψ​=∑r​ar​pr​=⟨ψ∣A∣ψ⟩.
(28)
Thus the expectation value is a probability-weighted average of eigenvalues, including all vectors in a degenerate eigenspace in its Pr​. In an orthonormal eigenbasis, ∣ψ⟩=∑j​cj​∣j⟩, this is ∑j​aj​∣cj​∣2, where repeated aj​ are allowed. The weighted average lies between the smallest and largest eigenvalues; it can lie in a gap between them. The statistical meaning and operator expression are connected in this way in the authored treatment of average energies.[ref]
If a nonzero vector ∣v⟩ has not been normalized, use ⟨v∣A∣v⟩/⟨v∣v⟩; the denominator is essential. A global phase cancels between the bra and ket, so ∣ψ⟩ and eiγ∣ψ⟩ have the same expectation value and outcome probabilities.
The outcome variance measures the spread about this mean, whereas the quantum uncertainty is its standard deviation:
Varψ​(A)=∑r​pr​(ar​−⟨A⟩ψ​)2=⟨A2⟩ψ​−⟨A⟩ψ2​=(ΔA)2.
(29)
For a pure state, zero variance means that ∣ψ⟩ lies entirely in one eigenspace. That eigenspace need not be one-dimensional. Knowing only a mean generally does not determine the entire outcome probability distribution.
For a mixed state, the same formulas use its density matrix ρ, a positive operator with trace one:
pr​=Tr(ρPr​),⟨A⟩ρ​=Tr(ρA),Varρ​(A)=Tr(ρA2)−Tr(ρA)2.
(30)
A pure state is the special case ρ=∣ψ⟩⟨ψ∣. For a quantum state ensemble ρ=∑k​wk​ρk​, the expectation value is ∑k​wk​⟨A⟩ρk​​. This linearity is useful when preparations vary between trials; different quantum state ensembles can have the same density matrix.
These formulas require no operator-domain qualifications in finite dimension. For an unbounded self-adjoint operator, the spectral theorem instead gives a spectral probability measure; a finite mean requires an integrable absolute first moment, and finite variance requires a finite second moment. Writing ⟨ψ∣A∣ψ⟩ as an operator inner product additionally requires ∣ψ⟩ in the operator domain of A. The quadratic form of a positive quantum Hamiltonian explains the useful wider form-domain version.

Prepare a fresh copy of the same quantum state for each trial and measure the same observable. If preparations and readouts are independent, the outcomes Xi​ are independent and identically distributed random variables with the Born rule probability distribution. Their sample mean is an unbiased estimator of the expectation value:
μ​N​=N1​∑i=1N​Xi​,E[μ​N​]=⟨A⟩,Var(μ​N​)=N(ΔA)2​,SE(μ​N​)=N​ΔA​.

The law of large numbers explains convergence of the sample mean, while the standard error describes its finite-sample spread. It takes four times as many independent trials to halve that standard error. This reduces estimation error; it does not reduce the quantum uncertainty of a single prepared copy.
For the spin expectation value, let n+​ and n−​ be the two outcome counts, with N=n+​+n−​. Then
μ​N​=2ℏ​Nn+​−n−​​,n+​∼Binomial(N,p+​),Pr(μ​N​=ℏ(Nk​−21​))=(kN​)p+k​(1−p+​)N−k.

The binomial distribution gives the exact sampling model. For θ=π/3, the standard error is ℏ3​/(4N​): approximately 0.1083ℏ for N=16 and 0.03827ℏ for N=128. A run can fluctuate away from the predicted mean even as its typical spread decreases.
Repeatedly measuring one surviving system is a different protocol. Under the ideal Lüders rule, outcome ar​ leaves Pr​∣ψ⟩/pr​​ when pr​>0. With no intervening change of observable or dynamics moving the state out of that eigenspace, the next projective measurement returns ar​ with certainty. Such a record is correlated and does not sample the original Born rule distribution independently. The quantum nondemolition measurement discussion describes this repeatability; fresh quantum state preparations supply the ensemble needed for the estimator above.
Stern-Gerlach expectation estimation
Words: 349
Estimating a quantum expectation value OurBigBook.com
A concrete idealized implementation uses a Stern-Gerlach experiment twice: a preparation filter along n=(sinθ,0,cosθ) passes only its plus spin channel, and a z analyzer resolves both output channels for many fresh atoms. This prepares the spin one-half along an axis state ∣ψθ​⟩. The authored apparatus description uses slit collimation, a nonuniform magnetic field with a pointed pole, and counters at the separated outputs.[ref] The two-channel spin one-half preparation and analyzer are described separately; the source's recombining “improved” apparatus is explicitly idealized, so the setup here is a proposed estimation model, not a report of observed counts.[ref]
Count every accepted analyzer event in its calibrated +z or −z channel and compute μ​N​ from the count difference. The magnetic field gradient separates trajectories through their magnetic moments; calibrated channel labels convert positions into spin eigenvalues. The readout is a population imbalance, not an intermediate trajectory carrying spin ℏcosθ/2. Beam position also depends on flight time and field geometry, so averaging raw positions alone does not establish a calibrated spin expectation value.
As controls, feed known ∣+z⟩ and ∣−z⟩ preparations to check the channel assignment and leakage, hold the analyzer axis fixed, and repeat short blocks to check preparation drift. Measure background counts and relative channel efficiencies. With efficiencies η+​ and η−​ and negligible background, the detected plus fraction is
p+det​=η+​p+​+η−​(1−p+​)η+​p+​​.
(36)
Unequal efficiencies bias the naive sample mean, even for arbitrarily many counts. For example, p+​=3/4, η+​=1, and η−​=1/2 give detected fraction 6/7 and naive mean 5ℏ/14, rather than ℏ/4. Background, overlapping beams, detector saturation, angle misalignment, unwanted internal states, and preparation correlations require a better measurement in quantum mechanics model. Increasing N only reduces the independent sampling contribution; it cannot remove these systematic errors. The selected preparation beam is the population being estimated, so losses in preparing it must be distinguished from losses in reading its two outcomes.

Hamiltonian (quantum mechanics) OurBigBook.com
A time-independent Hamiltonian evolves a state by the unitary operator U(t)=e−iHt/ℏ.
For a closed quantum system, unitary time evolution changes a quantum state through a unitary operator, preserving norms and inner products. For a time-independent self-adjoint Hamiltonian operator H, choose the initial time as zero:
iℏdtd​∣ψ(t)⟩=H∣ψ(t)⟩,∣ψ(t)⟩=U(t)∣ψ(0)⟩,U(t)=exp(−iHt/ℏ).
(40)
Here ℏ=h/(2π) is the reduced Planck constant. The same U(t) acts on every initial quantum state; it depends on the Hamiltonian operator and elapsed time, rather than the chosen preparation.[ref]
The self-adjointness of H makes the exponential a unitary operator. In finite dimension, conjugating its matrix exponential gives
U(t)†=exp(iHt/ℏ)=U(−t),U(t)†U(t)=UU†=I.
(41)
The two exponents commute because both are multiples of H. Hence, for any two initial vectors,
⟨Uϕ∣Uψ⟩=⟨ϕ∣U†U∣ψ⟩=⟨ϕ∣ψ⟩,∥Uψ∥=∥ψ∥.
(42)
This short proof explains why normalization survives, why orthogonality of initial vectors survives, and why the transition probability between two states evolved by the same U is unchanged. It does not require that a fixed measurement in quantum mechanics have time-independent probabilities: its measurement basis need not move with the quantum states.
For an unbounded self-adjoint operator, define the exponential through the spectral theorem, rather than assuming that its power series acts on every vector. It is a unitary operator on the entire Hilbert space; the strong Schrödinger equation holds for initial vectors in the operator domain D(H). For a density operator, unitary time evolution reads ρ(t)=U(t)ρ(0)U(t)†. It preserves eigenvalues and purity of a density operator, but can change its entries in a fixed basis.
The useful distinction is between conserving total probability and conserving each measurement's probabilities. A fixed energy spectrum supplies different ticking rates for different probability amplitudes. Their relative quantum phases can move the Bloch vector and create quantum interference even while every energy eigenstate population stays fixed. Qubit precession under a constant Hamiltonian makes this visible; Ramsey interferometry converts the accumulated relative quantum phase into a population difference that a simple readout can detect.

Ramsey interferometry uses two coherent pulses with a free interval between them: the first creates a quantum superposition, the interval accumulates relative quantum phase, and the second converts that quantum phase into measurement probabilities. Its attraction is that an ordinary population readout can reveal the quantum coherence hidden from an energy measurement during the free interval.
Here is an ideal qubit model with an explicit pulse convention. Let Ry​(θ)=exp(−iθσy​/2), prepare ∣0⟩, apply Ry​(π/2), evolve freely with Uϕ​=exp(−iϕσz​/2), and apply the inverse pulse Ry​(−π/2) before a computational-basis measurement. The first pulse gives ∣+⟩. Direct matrix multiplication gives

At ϕ=2π/3, the second pulse changes these probabilities to 1/4 and 3/4. If the two pulses have the same sign instead, the output labels interchange: the pulse convention is part of the prediction.
In a pulse experiment the phase is measured relative to the oscillator supplying the coherent pulses. In a rotating frame, write the free Hamiltonian operator as Hrot​=ℏδσz​/2 with signed angular frequency difference δ in the chosen labeling convention. A free interval T then accumulates ϕ=δT; changing the second pulse's phase changes the analysis direction. This comparison makes Ramsey interferometry useful for measuring frequency differences and diagnosing loss of quantum coherence.
For example, suppose the first pulse has prepared a density matrix with equal populations and transverse Bloch vector length 0≤V≤1:

Experimental contrast alone does not identify quantum decoherence: imperfect preparation, pulse errors and readout errors can also reduce it.

Ramsey interferometry OurBigBook.com
The 2002 experiment described in Manipulating the Quantum State of an Electrical Circuit demonstrates Ramsey interferometry in a circuit using superconductivity. An aluminum island between two small Josephson junctions and a larger readout Josephson junction formed the loop; a dilution refrigerator cooled it. Manipulation used the charge/flux bias point least sensitive to first-order fluctuations. Microwave pulse amplitude and duration were calibrated using Rabi oscillations. Two phase-coherent π/2 pulses then enclosed a variable free interval. A current pulse switched the large Josephson junction to finite voltage with state-dependent probability; a preamplifier and threshold discriminator counted repeated trials.[ref]
As a readout control, switching was tested against pulse height at thermal equilibrium. The Ramsey interferometry oscillation period agreed with inverse frequency detuning, supporting relative quantum phase accumulation against the external oscillator. The decaying envelope indicated finite quantum coherence, while reduced contrast was attributed provisionally to population relaxation during readout. This supports controlled coherent evolution over a finite interval, without establishing perfect isolation or identifying one exclusive noise mechanism.[ref]

Ramsey interferometry OurBigBook.com
A moving chemical atom or molecule can experience the two pulses of Ramsey interferometry by flying through two short oscillatory-field regions. Their common oscillator supplies the reference quantum phase; the flight between them supplies the interrogation time. The long interval need not contain a driving field. This turns a spatial apparatus into a coherent pulse sequence and makes narrow spectral lines possible without filling the entire flight path with a uniform oscillatory field.
Norman Foster Ramsey, Jr.'s 1950 paper calculates the two-state transition probability and averages it over molecular velocities. It is a theoretical investigation, rather than a report of an atomic clock's measured accuracy.[ref]
His 1989 lecture contrasts an electric-resonance apparatus photograph with a magnetic-resonance schematic. Coherent drive regions bracket a static-field flight region; state-dependent deflection converts transitions into detector changes, while differing flight times suppress side fringes.[ref]
The readout infers a change of internal quantum state through state-dependent transmission, as in the Rabi molecular beam magnetic resonance experiment. A useful control is to block one drive region: a narrow fringe requiring both interactions must disappear. Changing the second region's oscillation phase should move the fringe, whereas an incoherent background need not move. These are consequences of the model below, not additional historical measurements. A detector dip alone neither proves perfect preparation nor determines all apparatus-induced frequency shifts; cesium-beam clock procedure adds the controls needed for a practical atomic clock.
The publication sequence begins with Norman Foster Ramsey, Jr.'s 1949 article A New Molecular Beam Resonance Method, Physical Review 76, p. 996, published 1 October; the fuller theoretical paper followed in 1950.[ref]
NIST-7 supplied a practical realization: optical pumping moved caesium populations into the F=3 manifold, without isolating mF​=0. Two separated microwave interactions probed the clock transition; fluorescence detected transferred F=4 atoms. A synthesized reference, tied to a hydrogen maser, sampled opposite sides of resonance for feedback control. Beam reversal tested cavity quantum phase bias; independent velocity determinations checked motion corrections. The observed central fringe resolved the transition, but power-dependent velocity weighting and light shifts still required evaluation.[ref]

Ramsey spectroscopy measures a transition frequency by comparing the relative quantum phase acquired between two coherent interactions with the reference oscillator. In a beam, a state selector and apertures admit particular internal quantum states and trajectories; an analyzer and detector measure state-dependent transmission. In an optically prepared atomic clock, optical pumping and fluorescence can perform those functions. The preparation and readout determine which part of the beam contributes; they are not themselves the two coherent interactions.
For an ideal accepted particle, the first resonant half-duration Rabi pi pulse splits the probability amplitude between ∣g⟩ and ∣e⟩. The second combines two indistinguishable alternatives: a transition in the first region followed by no transition in the second, or the reverse. Their relative quantum phase depends on the dark flight and the drive oscillation phases. Adding probability amplitudes gives quantum interference; adding only the two alternatives' probabilities would erase the fringe. “Dark” means that the transverse drive is absent: a static magnetic field and the internal Hamiltonian operator can still act.
The useful separation is between pulse duration and phase-accumulation time. Short regions can share one coherent oscillator while a long drive-free interval resolves small frequency differences. A scan over reference frequency locates a fringe pattern; controlled changes of the second pulse's oscillation phase distinguish that coherent signal from phase-insensitive background. A reference scan must also identify the central fringe before atomic clock frequency lock, because neighboring fringes provide competing lock points.

For H=H0​+Hint​, the interaction picture moves the free evolution into operators and leaves states to evolve with HI​(t)=eiH0​tHint​e−iH0​t. Its evolution operator is the time-ordered Dyson series.
Time-reversal symmetry in quantum mechanics
Words: 160 Articles: 3
Unitary time evolution OurBigBook.com
A time-reversal operator T intertwines forward and backward evolution:
U(t)T=TU(−t).
(70)
It must be antiunitary in ordinary quantum mechanics. Its conjugate linearity sends i to −i, allowing it to commute with a time-reversal-invariant Hamiltonian rather than reversing the sign of its energy.
Quantum time-reversal operator (T^)
Words: 53
Time-reversal symmetry in quantum mechanics OurBigBook.com
A quantum time-reversal operator is an antiunitary operator reversing spatial momentum and angular momentum. For a time-reversal-invariant Hamiltonian operator, its conjugation of i makes it intertwine forward and backward unitary time evolution without reversing the energy spectrum. A scalar momentum eigenstate may transform as T^∣p⟩=eiχ(p)∣−p⟩. With unit-modulus phases and a complete normalized basis, expansion of arbitrary states proves antiunitarity.
Unitary time reversal reverses the energy spectrum
Words: 37
Time-reversal symmetry in quantum mechanics OurBigBook.com
If a unitary T satisfied U(t)T=TU(−t), differentiation at zero would give
HT=−TH.
(71)
It would map every energy E to −E. A Hamiltonian unbounded above would consequently be unbounded below and have no stable ground state.
Antiunitary time reversal preserves the energy spectrum
Words: 28
Time-reversal symmetry in quantum mechanics OurBigBook.com
For antiunitary T, conjugate linearity gives T(iψ)=−iTψ. Differentiating
U(t)T=TU(−t)
(72)
therefore yields HT=TH. Time reversal maps an energy eigenspace to itself and creates no negative-energy instability.
Rabi cycle (Pg→e​(t)=sin2(Ωt/2) on resonance)
Words: 2k Articles: 13
Unitary time evolution OurBigBook.com
A Rabi oscillation is a coherent oscillation of populations in a driven two-level quantum system.
A resonant drive can transfer a quantum state from one energy eigenstate to another and then bring its population back. This is unitary time evolution: the drive exchanges energy with the selected two-level system, while total probability stays one. One complete Rabi cycle has population period 2π/Ω; halfway through, a Rabi pi pulse transfers the whole population in the ideal model. This makes Rabi oscillations useful for calibrating resonant quantum control, preparing quantum superpositions and supplying the pulses of Ramsey interferometry.
Rotating-frame Rabi Hamiltonian (HR​=(Ω0​−ω)Sz​+ΩR​Sx​)
Words: 52
Rabi cycle OurBigBook.com
A circularly driven spin becomes time-independent after a rotation R=e−iωtSz​/ℏ. The transformed Hamiltonian operator is R†HR−iℏR†R˙, so the longitudinal frequency is shifted by −ω. This is an exact change of frame for a circular drive. The rotating-wave approximation is a separate approximation needed when a drive also contains a counterrotating component.
Circularly rotating magnetic drive (Ω=∣γ∣B1​)
Words: 56
Rabi cycle OurBigBook.com
For positive gyromagnetic ratio in static field Bz^, transverse components B1​cos(ωt+φ) and −B1​sin(ωt+φ) rotate with the spin precession. Their rotating-frame Hamiltonian operator is time independent, with transverse Rabi angular frequency Ω=γB1​. A linearly polarized field of peak amplitude Bpeak​ contains two oppositely rotating components and gives resonant Ω=∣γ∣Bpeak​/2 in the rotating-wave approximation. Negative gyromagnetic ratio requires opposite rotation sense.
Rabi frequency (Ω)
Words: 45
Rabi cycle OurBigBook.com
The coherent coupling frequency defined by the chosen driven two-level system Hamiltonian. With H=ℏ(−Δσz​+Ωσx​)/2, resonance gives population oscillations proportional to sin2(Ωt/2). Detuning replaces the oscillation frequency by Ω2+Δ2​ and reduces its contrast. Stating the Hamiltonian avoids factor-of-two ambiguities in the definition of Ω.
Resonance envelope of a Rabi transition (Pmax​(δ)=Ω2/(Ω2+δ2))
Words: 75
Rabi cycle OurBigBook.com
In the Driven two-level Rabi model, the transition probability is P(t)=Ω2sin2(Ω2+δ2​t/2)/(Ω2+δ2). Maximizing over time at each detuning gives a Lorentzian line shape, with first maximizing time π/Ω2+δ2​ and full width at half maximum 2∣Ω∣ in angular frequency. The amplitude parameter Ω must use the specified Rabi angular frequency convention.
This envelope differs from a spectrum obtained with a fixed pulse duration: optimizing the time separately removes the sine-squared factor, while fixing time retains it. A finite linewidth here describes detuning-limited transfer under coherent driving, without requiring dissipative decay.
Driven two-level Rabi model (Hrot​=ℏ[δσz​+Ω(cosϕσx​+sinϕσy​)]/2)
Words: 718 Articles: 6
Rabi cycle OurBigBook.com
Choose an isolated pair of energy levels, with ground state ∣g⟩=(0,1)T and excited state ∣e⟩=(1,0)T. Use the Pauli matrices in the ordered basis (∣e⟩,∣g⟩), so σz​=diag(1,−1). After subtracting the mean energy, prescribe the laboratory Hamiltonian operator
Hlab​(t)=2ℏω0​​σz​+ℏΩcos(ωt+ϕ)σx​,δ=ω0​−ω,Ω≥0.
(73)
The unperturbed energy gap is ℏω0​, the drive has angular frequency ω, and ϕ fixes its oscillation phase at the chosen time origin. All of ω0​, ω, the Rabi angular frequency Ω and the Rabi detuning δ are in radians per second; ordinary frequency is angular frequency divided by 2π. In particular, Ω here is the coefficient multiplying the cosine in Hlab​/ℏ, not twice that coefficient.
Write ∣ψlab​⟩=R(t)∣ψrot​⟩ with R(t)=exp(−iωtσz​/2). Transforming the Schrödinger equation gives Hrot​=R†Hlab​R−iℏR†R˙. The rotating-wave approximation drops terms at angular frequency 2ω, leaving
Hrot​=2ℏ​K,K=(δΩeiϕ​Ωe−iϕ−δ​),Ωeff​=Ω2+δ2​.
(74)
This approximation requires Ω,∣δ∣≪ω0​,ω, and an interaction duration over which omitted corrections remain small. It also assumes that other energy levels can be neglected. Resonance alone does not justify either assumption. An exactly co-rotating drive has no discarded counter-rotating component; the linearly oscillating laboratory drive above does.
The Pauli matrix multiplication law gives K2=Ωeff2​I. Separating even and odd terms of the matrix exponential therefore proves
Urot​(t)=Icos2Ωeff​t​−iΩeff​K​sin2Ωeff​t​,
(75)
with the continuous limit U=I when Ω=δ=0. Starting from ∣g⟩, the upper probability amplitude is −ie−iϕ(Ω/Ωeff​)sin(Ωeff​t/2). The Born rule gives
Pg→e​(t)=Ω2+δ2Ω2​sin2(2Ω2+δ2​t​).
(76)
The rotating transformation only changes the quantum phases of these basis states, so their laboratory populations are the same. Rabi detuning tilts the rotation axis of the Bloch vector: it increases the oscillation rate to Ωeff​ but caps the transferred population at Ω2/(Ω2+δ2). A fixed drive oscillation phase cancels from this single-pulse population when the initial state is ∣g⟩. It still fixes the relative quantum phase of a resulting quantum superposition and matters when another pulse supplies a phase reference.
Rabi vector (W)
Words: 59
Driven two-level Rabi model OurBigBook.com
For a rotating-frame two-state Hamiltonian operator H=ℏW⋅σ/2, the Bloch vector obeys R˙=W×R. Thus W specifies a rotation axis and angular speed. With detuning defined as drive frequency minus transition frequency and the lower state at positive Rz​, a phase-zero transverse drive can give W=(Ω,0,δ). Changing basis or detuning convention requires changing the corresponding signs consistently.
Equatorial reachability of a detuned spin pulse (∣Δ∣≤Ω)
Words: 78
Driven two-level Rabi model OurBigBook.com
For an initial pole of the Bloch sphere, one fixed-amplitude harmonic pulse detuned by Δ transfers at most Ω2/(Ω2+Δ2) of the population. A pure equatorial state requires half transfer, so some pulse duration reaches the equator exactly when ∣Δ∣≤Ω. Adjusting drive phase then selects its transverse azimuth. Exact inversion to the opposite pole is unavailable for nonzero detuning with that single fixed pulse. This is a restriction on the specified controls, rather than on composite-pulse or frequency-swept state preparation.
Laboratory phase of a resonant spin pulse (φend​=φ+ω0​τ)
Words: 59
Driven two-level Rabi model OurBigBook.com
With H0​=−ℏω0​σz​/2 and a co-rotating transverse magnetic drive of phase φ, an initial spin-up state becomes, up to common phase, cos(Ωτ/2)∣↑⟩+ie−i(φ+ω0​τ)sin(Ωτ/2)∣↓⟩. A quarter-turn pulse therefore prepares laboratory +x when φend​=π/2 and +y when φend​=0. Dropping the free-precession phase instead specifies targets in rotating axes. Transverse laboratory targets subsequently precess if the static field is retained.
Rabi angular frequency (Ω)
Words: 40
Driven two-level Rabi model OurBigBook.com
The Rabi angular frequency is the on-resonance population oscillation rate in the specified Driven two-level Rabi model. The rotating-frame off-diagonal Hamiltonian operator entry has magnitude ℏΩ/2. Stating this convention avoids a factor-of-two ambiguity between drive coefficients and oscillation rates. The generalized rate off resonance is Ωeff​=Ω2+δ2​.
Rabi detuning (δ=ω0​−ω)
Words: 42
Driven two-level Rabi model OurBigBook.com
The Rabi detuning is the unperturbed transition angular frequency minus the drive angular frequency in this convention. Its sign controls the longitudinal rotation of the Bloch vector; the single-pulse population formula is even in δ. Reversing the definition of Rabi detuning requires reversing its sign in the rotating-frame Hamiltonian operator as well.
Rabi pi pulse (Ωτπ​=π)
Words: 163
Driven two-level Rabi model OurBigBook.com
For a constant-amplitude square pulse on resonance, a Rabi pi pulse lasts τπ​=π/Ω and gives ∣g⟩↦−ie−iϕ∣e⟩ in the rotating frame. A half-duration pulse prepares (∣g⟩−ie−iϕ∣e⟩)/2​. The quantum pulse area Ωt determines these rotations only under the stated resonant, constant-axis assumptions; a detuned drive rotates about a different axis.
As an original numerical illustration, choose Ω=2π×1000 rads−1 and hence τπ​=0.500 ms. These are chosen model parameters, not historical apparatus settings. Holding that duration fixed gives
x=Ωδ​,Pπ​(x)=1+x2sin2[(π/2)1+x2​]​.
(77)
Thus Pπ​(0)=1, Pπ​(1)=21​sin2(π/2​)≃0.3166, and Pπ​(3​)=0. The last zero comes from completing a full rotation about the tilted axis, rather than switching the drive off. At zero Rabi detuning, doubling the pulse duration restores the ground-state population; continuous driving does not keep transferring population irreversibly.
Rabi molecular beam magnetic resonance experiment
Words: 587 Articles: 1
Rabi cycle OurBigBook.com
In 1938, Isidor Isaac Rabi, Jerrold Zacharias, Sidney Millman and Polykarp Kusch introduced molecular-beam magnetic resonance. Their 1939 account describes a heated oven, vacuum slits, inhomogeneous A/B magnetic fields with opposite gradients, and a uniform static C magnetic field. Conductors supplied transverse oscillatory radiofrequency (RF) fields. Transitions spoiled refocusing, reducing the tungsten-filament detector signal. Alignment compared A-only and B-only attenuation; C-field sweeps at fixed RF frequency limited oscillator pickup. Matching frequency/field ratios across compounds checked nuclear assignments. Magnetic field calibration limited absolute magnetic moments; weak intervening fields caused unwanted transitions.[ref]
The readout has a useful logical structure: A and the apertures admit trajectories correlated with a magnetic moment projection; B tests whether that projection has survived C. The two deflectors compensate for unchanged states, whereas a changed projection experiences a different force in B. A dip followed by recovery as the static magnetic field passes through resonance is therefore a population-sensitive signal. A comparison with RF absent or far from resonance is the natural baseline in this functional model; RF pickup, drift or background loss must not be mistaken for a state transition. A dip alone does not establish a pure initial quantum state or resolve an entire time-domain Rabi cycle.
This beam method measures transmitted particles after state-dependent deflection. The later bulk nuclear magnetic resonance methods of Felix Bloch and Edward Mills Purcell instead use a macroscopic sample and detect nuclear induction or RF absorption; NMR spectroscopy builds on that bulk setting. The common resonant coupling does not make their preparations or readouts interchangeable.[ref][ref]
Rabi transit-time and field averaging (τ=L/v)
Words: 284
Rabi molecular beam magnetic resonance experiment OurBigBook.com
For an ideal single transit, let the oscillatory magnetic field occupy a region of length L, take the longitudinal speed v constant, and neglect edge fields. Each molecule then experiences one square pulse of duration τ=L/v. This is one contiguous interaction region, distinct from the two separated pulses of Ramsey interferometry. The static magnetic field sets the selected transition gap; the transverse drive sets Rabi angular frequency. A change of RF frequency or static magnetic field changes Rabi detuning.
For an original ideal detector model, suppose every successful transition removes an otherwise accepted molecule and the incident beam occupies the lower state of the selected pair. With accepted no-transition signal S0​, constant background Sbg​, and effective loss contrast 0≤η≤1, write
S(δ)=Sbg​+S0​[1−ηP(δ)].
(78)
For identical trajectories P=Pg→e​(L/v), giving an intensity dip where transfer is largest. For real trajectory variation, a normalized joint probability density w(v,ϵ,Ω′) gives the static-offset model
P(δ)=∫0∞​dv∫−∞∞​dϵ∫0∞​dΩ′w(v,ϵ,Ω′)Ω′2+(δ+ϵ)2Ω′2​sin2[2vL​Ω′2+(δ+ϵ)2​],∫wdvdϵdΩ′=1.
(79)
Here ϵ is the trajectory's transition-frequency offset and Ω′ its drive strength, each in angular-frequency units. The weighting is for molecules accepted by the apparatus, rather than an assumed unfiltered oven distribution. In particular, designing ΩL/v0​=π does not produce a Rabi pi pulse for every speed: at 0.8v0​ and 1.2v0​ the resonant transfer probabilities are respectively sin2(5π/8)≃0.8536 and sin2(5π/12)≃0.9330.
Spread in transit times, static magnetic fields and drive amplitudes can reduce or smear oscillations without quantum decoherence on any individual trajectory. Even the single-transit square pulse has finite spectral width of order 1/τ in angular frequency. If the magnetic field varies substantially along one path, its Hamiltonian operator changes during the passage and the constant-offset average above must be replaced by a time-ordered exponential. Actual molecules may also have several coupled energy levels; the isolated pair and perfect loss discriminator are explicit idealizations of this model.

Bound state

Words: 513 Articles: 7
Quantum state OurBigBook.com
A bound state is a normalizable energy eigenstate spatially confined by a potential.

Half-line finite well

Words: 120 Articles: 1
Bound state OurBigBook.com
A one-dimensional well V=−V0​ on 0<x<a, with an infinite wall at zero and V=0 beyond a. For −V0​<E<0, the interior wavefunction is proportional to sinkx and the exterior decays as e−qx. Continuity gives kcotka=−q, where k2=2m(E+V0​)/ℏ2 and q2=−2mE/ℏ2. Its half-line finite-well bound-state count has a nonzero minimum depth, unlike a full-line attractive one-dimensional well.
Half-line finite-well bound-state count (ν>(n−21​)π)
Words: 63
Half-line finite well OurBigBook.com
For dimensionless depth ν=a2mV0​​/ℏ, each negative branch of zcotz=−ν2−z2​ gives one bound state. The nth state exists exactly when ν>(n−1/2)π. At equality its exterior decay constant vanishes and the state is not square integrable. In particular, exactly two bound states means 3π/2<ν≤5π/2. This strict lower and inclusive upper endpoint convention counts negative-energy eigenstates, excluding a zero-energy threshold solution.

Quantum bouncer (En​=Fℓzn​,ℓ=(ℏ2/(2mF))1/3)

Words: 171 Articles: 1
Bound state OurBigBook.com
A quantum particle above a hard reflecting wall in a linearly increasing potential V(x)=Fx for x>0. The Schrödinger equation reduces to the Airy equation. Decay at infinity selects Ai, while the wall requires Ai(−zn​)=0. Thus ψn​∝Ai(x/ℓ−zn​) and the energies are the displayed values. The nth state has n−1 interior nodes and a decaying tail beyond its classical turning point. A gravitational realization has F=mg; gravitational neutron bound-state transmission tests such confinement experimentally.
Gravitational neutron bound-state transmission
Words: 105
Quantum bouncer OurBigBook.com
A horizontal neutron-reflecting mirror supplies the lower boundary of a quantum bouncer, with the Earth's approximately linear gravitational potential above it. An absorber above the mirror removes neutrons with sufficient vertical extent. Scanning the mirror-absorber gap and counting transmitted neutrons probes the lowest allowed gravitational states. The 2002 work led by Valery V. Nesvizhevsky reported this confinement; a subsequent detailed report describes suppression below the lowest-state height.[ref][ref]
This is a count-versus-gap experiment, not a direct image of a wavefunction. Surface scattering, absorption and the incident vertical-motion distribution enter a quantitative transmission model.

Coulomb bound state (EN​=−mγ2/(2ℏ2N2))

Words: 209 Articles: 2
Bound state OurBigBook.com
A Coulomb bound state is a physical normalizable eigenfunction for an attractive potential V(r)=−γ/r, γ>0. For the usual regular boundary condition at the origin its energies are the displayed values, N=1,2,…. The spherically symmetric states have orbital angular momentum zero; series-termination quantization of the Coulomb radial equation constructs them as a polynomial times a decaying exponential. Square integrability on the punctured radial interval alone does not replace the physical condition at the origin.
Two-dimensional Coulomb bound state (E=−μκ2/[2ℏ2(nr​+∣m∣+1/2)2])
Words: 69
Coulomb bound state OurBigBook.com
For motion confined to a plane but retaining potential energy −κ/r, separation in polar coordinates gives angular wavefunctions eimϕ with integer m. The regular radial factor behaves as r∣m∣ at the origin. Removing this power and the decaying exponential function leaves an Generalized Laguerre polynomial differential equation. polynomial termination requires N=nr​+∣m∣+1/2, yielding the displayed energy. At fixed q=nr​+∣m∣, the spinless quantum degeneracy is 2q+1. This is not the logarithmic potential of electrostatics formulated entirely in two spatial dimensions.
Polynomial construction of hydrogen S states (cj+1​=[2b(j+1)−a]cj​/[(j+1)(j+2)])
Words: 74
Coulomb bound state OurBigBook.com
For a spherically symmetric bound state, write ψ=e−br∑cj​rj. The radial Coulomb equation gives the displayed recurrence. Choosing b=a/(2N) terminates it after degree N−1, producing a nonzero continuous polynomial times an exponentially decaying function. Its three-dimensional norm 4π∫0∞​r2∣ψ∣2dr is finite and can be normalized. The energy is −ℏ2a2/(8mN2). Continuity at the origin is compatible with the Coulomb cusp; no differentiability as a Cartesian radial function at the origin is asserted.
